There isn't really a seasonal pattern to it, but the shifts became much more noticeable after I moved in with my girlfriend and took on more design leadership roles at work.\n\nDoctor: Do you experience any other symptoms during these 'revved up' periods, such as increased talkativeness, distractibility, or involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences, like excessive spending or risky behaviors?\n\nPatient: Yes, during those wired times I've definitely made some impulsive purchases. I've put expensive camping gear, art supplies, and even a deposit for a last-minute trip on my credit card without checking my budget first. It's only later on that I start stressing about how I'm going to pay it all off.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how quickly you shift from these 'revved up' periods to the low spells, and do you ever experience both extremes at the same time or very close together?\n\nPatient: The revved-up phases usually last for just a few days, and then I'll sink into the longer low spells that can hang around for weeks or months. I don't experience both of those extremes at the same time; they are separate, alternating parts of a cycle that's been happening off and on for about a year.\n\nDoctor: During these 'revved up' periods, do you feel that your mood is irritable or if you're more likely to be exceptionally happy or euphoric?\n\nPatient: It's actually a mix of both. I'll feel unusually amped up and upbeat, like every single thing is a great idea, but at the same time, I get easily irritated and set off by small things, like my girlfriend questioning my new projects.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there are any periods of normal mood in between these 'revved up' and low spells, or do you tend to shift directly from one extreme to the other?\n\nPatient: I'm not completely sure, to be honest. I haven't paid close enough attention to notice if there are truly \"normal\" periods in between, or if I just slide directly from one phase right into the other.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel like you're back to your normal self, with a stable mood, between these episodes of feeling 'revved up' and the low spells, or is it more like you're constantly shifting between these two extremes?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure, because over the last year it feels like I've been constantly shifting or just stuck in that low spell. I don't really recall having many periods where I felt truly \"normal\" or stable in between.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any specific times in the past year when you felt completely stable and normal, without either the 'revved up' or low spell symptoms, even if it was just for a short period?\n\nPatient: Honestly, it's really hard to recall any specific times over the past year where I felt completely stable or normal. The low feelings have been hanging around in some form for most of the past year, and these cycles of getting revved up and then sinking back down have just been happening off and on the whole time.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have experienced any period, regardless of length, within the past year where your mood was consistently stable, without any episodes of being 'revved up' or in a low spell, or has it been a constant fluctuation between these states?\n\nPatient: It has felt like a pretty constant cycle without much stable ground over the past year. The low spell has been hanging around in some form for most of the year, only occasionally interrupted by those brief, highly-energized \"revved up\" phases. It's just been a continuous loop of those two states.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least two months in your life, not just the past year, where you felt consistently stable and free from both the 'revved up' and low spell symptoms?\n\nPatient: I'm not quite sure, to be honest. It's really hard to recall a solid two-month block in my life where I felt completely stable and free of both the highs and the lows. In contrast, the low spells are much longer, with this current low period dragging on in some form for most of the past year.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a distinct period of hypomanic symptoms, such as increased energy and reduced need for sleep, that lasted for at least four consecutive days?\n\nPatient: Yes, I definitely have those periods where I feel extremely amped up and buzzing with energy. It feels like I've just been constantly cycling between the highs and lows without any real, steady break in between.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever experienced a full year in your life without any significant episodes of 'revved up' or low spell symptoms, where you felt consistently stable and normal throughout?"

It's the total opposite of my low spells, where I feel completely sluggish, foggy, and lose interest in everything.\n\nDoctor: Can you estimate how often these 'revved up' periods and low spells occur, and do they seem to follow a pattern or cycle, such as happening at specific times of the year or in response to particular events?\n\nPatient: These cycles have been happening off and on for about a year, with the revved-up phases lasting just a few days and the low spells dragging on for most of the year. There isn't really a seasonal pattern to it, but the shifts became much more noticeable after I moved in with my girlfriend and took on more design leadership roles at work.\n\nDoctor: Do you experience any other symptoms during these 'revved up' periods, such as increased talkativeness, distractibility, or involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences, like excessive spending or risky behaviors?\n\nPatient: Yes, during those wired times I've definitely made some impulsive purchases. I've put expensive camping gear, art supplies, and even a deposit for a last-minute trip on my credit card without checking my budget first. It's only later on that I start stressing about how I'm going to pay it all off.\n\nDoctor: Can you tell me more about how quickly you shift from these 'revved up' periods to the low spells, and do you ever experience both extremes at the same time or very close together?\n\nPatient: The revved-up phases usually last for just a few days, and then I'll sink into the longer low spells that can hang around for weeks or months. I don't experience both of those extremes at the same time; they are separate, alternating parts of a cycle that's been happening off and on for about a year.\n\nDoctor: During these 'revved up' periods, do you feel that your mood is irritable or if you're more likely to be exceptionally happy or euphoric?\n\nPatient: It's actually a mix of both. I'll feel unusually amped up and upbeat, like every single thing is a great idea, but at the same time, I get easily irritated and set off by small things, like my girlfriend questioning my new projects.\n\nDoctor: Can you clarify if there are any periods of normal mood in between these 'revved up' and low spells, or do you tend to shift directly from one extreme to the other?\n\nPatient: I'm not completely sure, to be honest. I haven't paid close enough attention to notice if there are truly \"normal\" periods in between, or if I just slide directly from one phase right into the other.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel like you're back to your normal self, with a stable mood, between these episodes of feeling 'revved up' and the low spells, or is it more like you're constantly shifting between these two extremes?\n\nPatient: I'm not entirely sure, because over the last year it feels like I've been constantly shifting or just stuck in that low spell. I don't really recall having many periods where I felt truly \"normal\" or stable in between.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any specific times in the past year when you felt completely stable and normal, without either the 'revved up' or low spell symptoms, even if it was just for a short period?\n\nPatient: Honestly, it's really hard to recall any specific times over the past year where I felt completely stable or normal. The low spells have been hanging around in some form for most of the year, and otherwise I've just been cycling back and forth between those low periods and the short, revved-up phases.\n\nDoctor: Can you think of any instance in the past year where you had at least two months of relatively stable mood without significant episodes of being 'revved up' or in a low spell?\n\nPatient: No, I definitely haven't had a solid two-month stretch of feeling stable this past year. The low, dragging feelings have been there in some form for most of the year, and whenever I wasn't feeling down, I was usually in one of those revved-up phases. There really hasn't been any room for a normal, stable baseline.\n\nDoctor: Have you experienced any distinct periods of at least two months where your mood was consistently stable and free from both the 'revved up' and low spell symptoms, or has it been a constant fluctuation between these two states over the past year?\n\nPatient: I'm not quite sure, and I haven't tracked things closely enough to know if I've had a full two-month stretch of feeling completely stable. It really just feels like I've been riding this rollercoaster of ups and downs, or dealing with those low feelings pretty consistently, over the past year.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm if there has been any period, no matter how brief, within the past year where you felt completely free of both the 'revved up' and low spell symptoms for at least a few weeks?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't really had a clear period of even a few weeks where I felt completely normal. The low feelings have been hanging around in some form for most of the past year, and these cycles of getting revved up and then sinking back down have just been happening off and on the whole time.\n\nDoctor: Can you confirm whether you have experienced any period, regardless of length, within the past year where your mood was consistently stable, without any episodes of being 'revved up' or in a low spell, or has it been a constant fluctuation between these states?\n\nPatient: It has felt like a pretty constant cycle without much stable ground over the past year. It's just been a continuous loop of those two states.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least two months in your life, not just the past year, where you felt consistently stable and free from both the 'revved up' and low spell symptoms?\n\nPatient: I'm not quite sure, to be honest.
